title: A Forgotten Forest Experiment Grew Giant Trees
summary:
In Australia, people have argued for years about forests. Some want them fully protected. Others want to cut trees for wood and jobs.

In the late 1980s, the state of Victoria started a big experiment in its mountain ash forests. Mountain ash trees are some of the tallest trees in the world. In some areas, every tree was cut. In "heavily thinned" areas, 50 to 70 percent of the trees were cut. Other areas were left alone.

Later, the experiment was forgotten. Then in 2014, researchers from the University of Melbourne visited and were amazed.

In the thinned areas, the trees left behind had grown huge. The biggest were 20 percent wider than the biggest trees in untouched forest. The thinned forest also stored as much carbon as untouched forest, or more.

Cameras found rare Leadbeater's possums in every cut area the team checked, but none in untouched areas.
why_it_matters: It shows that careful forest care might help people get wood while still helping trees and animals.
